verdict: The sources confirm that children often have low fiber intake and that school programs lack plant-based policies, but they do not provide specific data on the fiber-to-calorie ratios of government-subsidized meals.
caveat: Most evidence regarding the specific health effects of fiber in children is currently inconsistent or lacking from high-quality clinical trials.
caption:
Standardized school meals are under scrutiny for their impact on children's health.

Research shows that most children consume fiber well below recommended levels, yet clinical data on how specific fiber-to-calorie ratios in school meals affect insulin resistance is currently lacking or inconsistent.
